newsitem.title: bangladesh: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - April 29.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - April 29.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
Three people were killed and 115 others injured when no'westers hit northern Natore and Kushtia districts on Monday.

The Hong Kong Bank, Saudi British Bank and Arab Bangladesh Bank have signed a "Dial-A-Remittance" agreement under which will further facilitate Bangladeshis working in Saudi Arabia remit their money home.
Police in two separate drives recovered a large number of illegal fireamrs, many turned junks, in the capital city on Monday, and arrested 16 people in this connection.
The central bank governor, Lutfar Rahman Sarkar, said on Monday that the country's GDP growth rate might exceed 5.5 percent during the current 1996-97 fiscal year, ending June.
Bangladesh is going to enter the European labour market in May when a batch of formally recruited Bangladeshi workers for a European construction company will fly for the Austrian capital Vienna.
In a bit resolve the crisis in his Jatiya Party, former President Hussain Muhammad Ershad has agreed to withdraw expulsion order on party presidium member Kazi Zafar Ahmed.
A Food Security Mission of the UN Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO) found significant socio-economic and agricultural progress in Bangladesh, but a dismal state of food security.
The International Jute Organisation (IJO) undertook twenty projects involving $7.66 million to revamp the global jute economy combating the intrusive synthetics. REUTER
